answer: Let zephyr, dune, and pearl denote trusted roots. Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, so a Sybil cluster with few weighted edges to those roots has low conductance: only a small fraction of walk mass can enter it. Under bounded-degree and root-separation assumptions, conductance and min-cut bounds therefore limit the cluster’s aggregate voting weight, rather than allowing many internally connected identities to amplify it without limit.
